page: The Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose cloud instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores and 8 threads of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor provides 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside hardware support for vector instruction extensions including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support) and cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

Hardware provisioning couples the dedicated CPU cores with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced general-purpose allocation ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, contains no discrete graphics accelerators, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 72.12 GB/sec for large block reads and 41.41 GB/sec for writes.

Benchmark results reveal strong single-threaded performance profiles. The instance placed in the top tier for stress-ng single-core compute, single-threaded gzip compression at 39.78 GB/sec, single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 17.59 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing. Multi-core performance is aligned with standard mid-tier server baselines, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7445.0, a PassMark CPU score of 18506.84, and Redis SET throughput of 15.71 million operations per second. In small-scale machine learning benchmarks, lightweight 135M model text generation achieved a strong 324.23 tokens per second, though medium 7B model prompt processing settled in the lower 25% bracket at 27.21 tokens per second.

With its 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration and dedicated hardware cores, the vx1-g-8c-32g operates cost-efficiently for balanced multi-threaded services. The limited 1 GB local NVMe disk indicates that persistent data stores will necessitate external networked block storage. The system is suited for medium web serving pipelines, microservice backends, text data processing, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
description: Vultr vx1-g-8c-32g is a general-purpose cloud instance from the VX1 Cloud Compute series, equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical AMD EPYC cores at 2.0 GHz and 32.0 GB of memory. The instance features AVX-512 vector support, 32 MB of L3 cache, 1 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, and no GPU accelerators. Benchmarks highlight upper-tier execution in single-core compute, text processing, and compression routines like gzip and bzip3, while multi-core compute, Redis operations, and memory bandwidth maintain average mid-tier cloud metrics. Small language model inference delivers strong text generation rates, though prompt processing on larger models is constrained by the 2.0 GHz base frequency. Given the nominal local disk allocation, it is intended for memory-balanced compute tasks, text processing, web serving, and CI/CD compilation requiring external volume storage.
